question: Which living ingredient makes bread dough rise?
note: Yeast feeds on sugars and releases carbon dioxide, which inflates the dough.

question: What plant makes up most of a giant panda’s diet?
note: Wild giant pandas spend much of the day eating bamboo.

question: In tennis scoring, what does “love” mean?
note: Love is the standard tennis term for a score of zero.

question: Which river flows beneath London’s Tower Bridge?
note: Tower Bridge crosses the River Thames in central London.

question: Who sings lead on the Beatles’ 1966 single “Yellow Submarine”?
note: Ringo Starr sings the lead vocal; the other Beatles join the choruses.

question: After breathing normal air, we exhale mostly which gas?
note: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of inhaled air and remains the largest part of exhaled air.

question: What is allspice made from?
note: Allspice is the dried, unripe berry of the Pimenta dioica tree.

question: Penguins expel their salt glands’ secretions through what?
note: Their salt glands drain into the nasal passages, so excess salt leaves through the nostrils.

question: In Carroll’s Alice in Wonderland, the Duchess’s baby turns into what?
note: Alice carries the baby away before it transforms into a pig.

question: Ming, the animal dated to 507 years old, was what?
note: Ming was an ocean quahog clam collected near Iceland.

question: Margarine’s original French recipe got its main fat from what?
note: Hippolyte Mège-Mouriès made early margarine largely from beef fat.

question: At Heinz’s 1869 launch, what was its first bottled product?
note: Henry Heinz first sold his mother’s grated horseradish in clear bottles.

question: What color are Dorothy’s magic slippers in the 1939 Wizard of Oz?
note: The film changed the book’s silver shoes to ruby slippers to exploit Technicolor.

question: A leaf from which tree appears on Canada’s national flag?
note: The flag centers a stylized red maple leaf.

question: The fuzzy side of a Velcro fastener is covered in tiny what?
note: One strip has hooks; the softer strip has loops for those hooks to catch.

question: Which part of your eye changes the size of your pupil?
note: Muscles in the iris constrict or dilate the pupil to control incoming light.

question: The Taj Mahal’s main white marble building was built as what?
note: Shah Jahan commissioned the complex as a mausoleum for Mumtaz Mahal.

question: What bird’s head forms the handle of Mary Poppins’ umbrella?
note: Mary Poppins carries an umbrella with a talking parrot-head handle.

question: In 1971’s Willy Wonka, the machine that rejects Veruca tests what?
note: The Eggdicator judges golden chocolate eggs as good or bad.

question: In classic Clue, what must you still try to do after a wrong accusation?
note: You stop moving and suggesting, but must still show cards to disprove others’ suggestions.

question: What does a tape measure’s sliding end hook compensate for?
note: The hook slides by its own thickness so inside and outside measurements agree.

question: What gives ordinary aluminum foil its shiny and dull sides?
note: Two sheets are rolled together at the final pass. The sides touching the rollers become shiny.

question: Which kitchen tool did Jackson Pollock use to squeeze paint onto canvas?
note: Pollock used hardened brushes, sticks, and even a kitchen baster to drip and pour paint.

question: In soccer, a legal throw-in goes directly into your own goal. What next?
note: A goal cannot be scored directly from a throw-in. Into your own goal means a corner kick.

question: What was the fake blood in the shower scene of Psycho made from?
note: The black-and-white film used chocolate syrup because its tone and flow read well on camera.

question: Which candy did E.T. follow in E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial?
note: Elliott lays a trail of Reese’s Pieces to coax E.T. out of hiding.

question: What make of car is the time machine in Back to the Future?
note: Doc Brown builds the time machine from a stainless-steel DeLorean DMC-12.

question: David Bowie was born with which surname?
note: He was born David Robert Jones and changed his stage name to avoid confusion with Davy Jones.

question: What was the working title of the Beatles song “Yesterday”?
note: McCartney used “Scrambled Eggs” as a placeholder while developing the melody.

question: The name ABBA is formed from what?
note: ABBA takes one initial from Agnetha, Björn, Benny, and Anni-Frid.

question: Which actor provided Darth Vader’s speaking voice in the original Star Wars trilogy?
note: David Prowse played Vader physically, while James Earl Jones supplied the voice.

question: Toy Story was the first feature film made entirely with what?
note: Pixar’s 1995 release was the first fully computer-animated feature film.

question: In golf, what does a birdie mean?
note: A birdie is a score of one stroke under par on a hole.

question: How many feathers are traditionally used in a badminton shuttlecock?
note: Competition feather shuttlecocks use 16 feathers fixed into the cork base.

question: What color jersey marks the overall leader of the Tour de France?
note: The race leader wears the yellow jersey, or maillot jaune.

question: How many balls make up a standard over in modern cricket?
note: An over consists of six valid deliveries by one bowler.

question: Why does a volleyball libero wear a contrasting jersey?
note: The different jersey lets officials track the libero’s special substitution and position rules.

question: How many points is the black ball worth in snooker?
note: The black is the highest-value color ball at seven points.

question: The modern marathon distance is 26 miles plus how many yards?
note: The official distance is 26 miles 385 yards, or 42.195 kilometers.

question: What is Wimbledon’s playing surface?
note: Wimbledon is the only tennis Grand Slam still played on grass.

question: Botanically, peanuts belong to which family?
note: Peanuts grow in pods and belong to the legume family with peas and beans.

question: Capers are usually pickled parts of a plant. Which parts?
note: Capers are unopened flower buds from the caper bush.

question: Which spice is the dried stigma of a flower?
note: Saffron consists of hand-picked stigmas from the saffron crocus.

question: Nutmeg and mace come from what relationship?
option_b: One tree’s seed and seed covering
answer: One tree’s seed and seed covering
note: Nutmeg is the seed; mace is the lacy red covering around that seed.

question: Traditional Worcestershire sauce contains which fish?
note: Anchovies ferment with vinegar, molasses, tamarind, and seasonings in the classic sauce.

question: What does the Italian name tiramisu roughly mean?
note: The name comes from an Italian phrase meaning “pick me up” or “cheer me up.”

question: The modern chocolate chip cookie was created at which inn?
note: Ruth Wakefield developed the cookie at Massachusetts’s Toll House Inn.

question: Before small table forks caught on in Europe, forks were mainly used for what?
note: Ancient forks were largely cooking tools; small personal eating forks spread much later.

question: How many hearts does an octopus have?
note: Two hearts pump blood to the gills and one pumps it around the body.

question: What unusual shape are wombat droppings?
note: Wombats produce cube-shaped droppings due to the changing elasticity of their intestines.

question: What color is a polar bear’s skin under its fur?
note: Polar bears have black skin beneath translucent, light-scattering fur.

question: A giraffe has how many neck vertebrae?
note: Like most mammals, a giraffe has seven neck vertebrae, each one greatly elongated.

question: Flamingos get their pink color mainly from what?
note: Carotenoid pigments from algae and small crustaceans color their feathers.

question: Which planet has a day longer than its year?
note: Venus rotates once in about 243 Earth days but orbits the Sun in about 225.

question: What color can sunsets appear on Mars?
note: Fine Martian dust scatters light so the sky near the setting Sun can look blue.

question: Which planet is hottest, despite not being closest to the Sun?
note: Venus’s thick carbon-dioxide atmosphere traps enough heat to make it hotter than Mercury.

question: What does the “WD” in WD-40 stand for?
note: The product name records “Water Displacement” and the successful 40th formula.

question: Pencil “lead” is actually made mainly from what?
note: Pencil cores use graphite mixed with clay, not metallic lead.

question: Bubble Wrap was first marketed as what?
note: Its inventors first tried selling the sealed-air plastic sheets as textured wallpaper.

question: What does ZIP in ZIP Code stand for?
note: The U.S. Postal Service introduced the Zone Improvement Plan code in 1963.

question: Big Ben is properly the nickname of what?
note: Big Ben names the Great Bell; the tower itself is Elizabeth Tower.

question: Which country lies in all four hemispheres?
note: Kiribati crosses both the equator and the 180-degree meridian.

question: What is the world’s deepest lake?
note: Siberia’s Lake Baikal reaches about 1,620 meters at its deepest point.

question: The Statue of Liberty’s outer skin is made from what metal?
note: Thin copper sheets form the exterior; oxidation created the green patina.

question: What was the first music video shown on MTV?
note: MTV launched on August 1, 1981, with the Buggles video Video Killed the Radio Star.

question: The film sound-effect technique called Foley is named after a person with what first name?
note: Sound-effects artist Jack Foley pioneered the synchronized performance technique that bears his name.

question: How tall is an Oscar statuette?
note: The Academy Award statuette stands 13.5 inches tall and weighs 8.5 pounds.

question: Which film first used the famous Wilhelm scream sound effect?
note: The scream was originally recorded for the 1951 film Distant Drums before later receiving its nickname.

question: What song does Sam repeatedly play in Casablanca?
note: Sam plays Herman Hupfeld's As Time Goes By for Ilsa and later for Rick.

question: Which 1983 film was the first theatrical release to use the THX sound system?
note: THX debuted with Return of the Jedi at the film's 1983 premiere.

question: What nickname did the crew give the mechanical shark in Jaws?
note: The Jaws crew called its troublesome mechanical shark Bruce.

question: Which Disney animated feature was the first released in CinemaScope?
note: Lady and the Tramp became Disney's first animated feature produced in the widescreen CinemaScope format.

question: How far is a soccer penalty mark from the goal line?
note: The penalty mark sits 12 yards from the midpoint between the goalposts.

question: How many double stitches are on a regulation Major League baseball?
note: A regulation baseball has 108 double stitches sewn into its cover.

question: How high is the top edge of a regulation basketball rim?
note: Basketball rules place the rim 10 feet above the playing floor.

question: What is the official height of a table-tennis net?
note: The net assembly must be 15.25 centimeters high along its entire length.

question: How many sides does baseball's home plate have?
note: Home plate is a five-sided slab with a 17-inch edge facing the pitcher.

question: How long may a golfer search for a lost ball under the current rules?
note: A ball is lost if it is not found within three minutes after the search begins.

question: What is the maximum number of clubs a golfer may carry during a round?
note: The Rules of Golf limit a player to 14 clubs during a round.

question: A pineapple develops from roughly what structure?
note: A pineapple is a multiple fruit formed as many individual flowers fuse together.

question: Vanilla beans are the fruits of what kind of plant?
note: Commercial vanilla comes from the cured fruits of climbing orchids in the genus Vanilla.

question: Where does a cashew nut grow on its fruit?
note: The cashew seed hangs in a shell from the bottom of the fleshy cashew apple.

question: Cream of tartar is a crystalline by-product of making what?
note: Cream of tartar is purified potassium bitartrate deposited during wine fermentation and aging.

question: What physical test is traditionally used to sort ripe cranberries?
note: Sound cranberries bounce, allowing damaged berries to be separated by bounce-board sorters.

question: What gives tonic water its characteristic bitterness?
note: Tonic water is flavored with the bitter alkaloid quinine.

question: Which fruit supplies the enzyme bromelain used as a meat tenderizer?
note: Pineapple tissues contain bromelain, a mixture of protein-digesting enzymes.

question: An owl's eyes are shaped more like what than balls?
note: An owl has elongated, tube-shaped eyes held rigidly in bony structures called sclerotic rings.

question: Which marine mammal has the densest fur?
note: Sea otters can have up to about one million hairs per square inch of fur.

question: Butterflies primarily taste with receptors located where?
note: Taste receptors on a butterfly's feet help it identify suitable food and host plants.

question: What color can reindeer eyes turn during the Arctic winter?
note: Reindeer tapeta change from gold in summer to deep blue in winter to improve low-light sensitivity.

question: How often does a typical three-toed sloth descend from its tree to defecate?
note: Three-toed sloths usually make a risky descent to the forest floor about once a week.

question: Which bird has nostrils located near the tip of its bill?
note: Unlike most birds, kiwis have nostrils near the tip of their long bills.

question: What is the only venomous primate known to science?
note: Slow lorises produce venom from a gland on the upper arm and deliver it through a bite.

question: At sea-level pressure, how hot can a lightning channel become?
note: A lightning channel can heat surrounding air to roughly 30,000 degrees Celsius.

question: Which element was detected in the Sun before it was found on Earth?
note: Helium was identified in the Sun's spectrum in 1868 before terrestrial helium was isolated.

question: What is the smallest bone in the human body?
note: The stirrup-shaped stapes in the middle ear is the body's smallest bone.

question: What is absolute zero on the Celsius scale?
note: Absolute zero is exactly 0 kelvin, equivalent to -273.15 degrees Celsius.

question: What is the temperature of water's triple point?
note: Pure water's solid, liquid, and vapor phases coexist at 0.01 degrees Celsius at the triple point.

question: Why can no ordinary sound be heard in a vacuum?
option_b: Sound needs matter to carry vibrations
answer: Sound needs matter to carry vibrations
note: Sound is a mechanical wave and needs particles in a medium to transmit its vibrations.

question: Roughly how much DNA do humans and chimpanzees share?
note: Comparisons of directly alignable DNA sequences put human-chimpanzee similarity at about 98.8 percent.

question: Which country has the world's only national flag not shaped as a quadrilateral?
note: Nepal's flag consists of two joined triangular pennants rather than a four-sided field.

question: Which sea has no land coastline?
note: The Sargasso Sea is bounded by rotating Atlantic currents rather than by land.

question: Which country has three official capital cities?
note: South Africa divides its executive, legislative, and judicial seats among Pretoria, Cape Town, and Bloemfontein.

question: What is Bolivia's constitutional capital?
note: Sucre is Bolivia's constitutional capital, while La Paz is the seat of government.

question: Which sovereign country is entirely above 1,000 meters in elevation?
note: Every part of Lesotho lies above 1,000 meters, giving it the world's highest lowest point.

question: Which European country shares its longest land border with Brazil?
note: French Guiana makes France's border with Brazil longer than any of France's European borders.

question: Ecuador takes its name from which geographic feature?
note: The country's Spanish name means equator, the line that crosses its territory.

question: How many letter tiles are in an English-language Scrabble set?
note: The standard English Scrabble distribution contains 100 tiles, including two blanks.

question: How many possible arrangements does a standard 3-by-3 Rubik's Cube have?
note: A standard Rubik's Cube has 43,252,003,274,489,856,000 possible configurations.

question: Green Eggs and Ham was written using how many different words?

question: Who illustrated the original published edition of Alice's Adventures in Wonderland?
note: John Tenniel supplied the 42 illustrations for the 1865 published edition.

question: In standard Monopoly, what happens when a player rolls doubles three times in one turn?
note: Three consecutive doubles in one turn send the player immediately to Jail.

question: Which chess piece may jump over other pieces?
note: The knight is the only standard chess piece whose move can pass over intervening pieces.

question: What shape is the original Pac-Man character based on?
note: Creator Toru Iwatani said the character's shape was inspired by a pizza with one slice removed.

question: Why do many ballpoint pen caps have a hole through the top?
note: The hole allows some airflow if the cap is accidentally swallowed and blocks the airway.

question: What was the tiny fifth pocket on blue jeans originally designed to hold?
note: Levi Strauss describes the small pocket as a watch pocket made for pocket watches.

question: What was the first product scanned with a UPC barcode in a store?
note: A pack of Wrigley's Juicy Fruit gum became the first retail item scanned by UPC in 1974.

question: Post-it Notes resulted from an attempt to invent what?
note: 3M scientist Spencer Silver was trying to make a strong adhesive when he created a weak reusable one.

question: The raised bumps on the F and J keyboard keys identify what?
note: The tactile marks let touch typists locate the home-row index-finger keys without looking.

question: What prevents microwaves from escaping through an oven door's viewing window?
note: The perforated metal screen blocks microwave wavelengths while its smaller holes pass visible light.

question: What kind of machine was the QWERTY keyboard layout developed for?
note: Christopher Latham Sholes developed QWERTY for his early practical typewriter.

question: The Bayeux Tapestry is technically what kind of textile?
note: Its scenes are stitched in wool thread onto linen, making it an embroidery rather than a true tapestry.

question: George Washington's dentures were never made from which commonly claimed material?
note: Washington's dentures used materials including ivory, metal, and human or animal teeth, but not wood.

question: Ancient Tyrian purple dye came mainly from what animals?
note: Mediterranean craftspeople extracted Tyrian purple from secretions of predatory murex sea snails.

question: What covered the Great Pyramid's rough core when it was new?
note: Smooth white Tura limestone casing blocks originally covered the pyramid's core masonry.

question: Where is the sling on Michelangelo's David?
option_a: Across his back and left hand
answer: Across his back and left hand
note: David holds the sling over his left shoulder and down through his left hand.

question: How tall was Napoleon Bonaparte according to a French medical measurement at his death?
note: Converting the old French measurement puts Napoleon near 5 feet 6 inches in modern British units.

question: The Liberty Bell's visible crack grew beyond repair during what event?
note: The bell's final major crack widened while it rang for Washington's birthday in 1846.

question: What is the figure on an Academy Award statuette holding?
note: The statuette depicts a knight holding a crusader sword while standing on a film reel.

question: At the 1939 Academy Awards, how was Walt Disney honored for Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs?
option_b: With one full-size and seven miniature statuettes
answer: With one full-size and seven miniature statuettes
note: Shirley Temple presented Disney with one standard Oscar accompanied by seven miniature statuettes.

question: Which member of Queen wrote "Another One Bites the Dust"?
note: Queen bassist John Deacon wrote the song and its famous bass line.

question: The THX cinema sound heard before films is officially called what?
note: THX calls its swelling audio trademark the Deep Note.

question: Which instrument plays the opening solo in George Gershwin's "Rhapsody in Blue"?
note: The work opens with a clarinet trill that climbs into a long glissando.

question: What was Mickey Mouse's first spoken phrase in a cartoon?
note: Mickey first spoke in The Karnival Kid, where his first words were "Hot dogs!"

question: Which singer wrote the Dolly Parton hit "I Will Always Love You"?
note: Dolly Parton wrote and first recorded the song years before Whitney Houston's version.

question: On Sesame Street, what is the Count's full title and name?
note: The number-loving vampire Muppet is formally named Count von Count.

question: Which film introduced the song "When You Wish Upon a Star"?
note: Jiminy Cricket sings the song at the beginning of Disney's Pinocchio.

question: How many strikes are rolled in a perfect ten-pin bowling game?
note: A 300 game needs strikes in all ten frames plus two bonus deliveries in the tenth.

question: May a chess king legally move onto a square attacked by an opponent?
note: A king may not move onto an attacked square because that would leave it in check.

question: How many points is a try worth in rugby union before any conversion?
note: World Rugby awards five points for grounding the ball for a try.

question: In baseball, a fly ball that strikes a foul pole is ruled what?
note: The foul poles stand in fair territory, so a fair fly striking one above the fence is a home run.

question: In boxing, where must the standing boxer wait during a knockdown count?
note: The boxer who scored the knockdown must go to the farthest neutral corner during the count.

question: In table tennis, what happens when an otherwise legal serve clips the net and lands correctly?
note: That serve is a let, so no point is scored and the service is taken again.

question: After a touchdown in American football, how far is a successful kick worth?
note: The kick try after a touchdown scores one additional point.

question: In Formula 1, what does a black flag with an orange circle tell a driver?
option_c: The car has a mechanical problem
answer: The car has a mechanical problem
note: The black-and-orange flag warns that a car has a mechanical problem likely to endanger others.

question: In basketball, how many personal fouls disqualify an NBA player?
note: An NBA player is disqualified after committing a sixth personal foul.

question: Which part of a cinnamon tree becomes the familiar spice?
note: Cinnamon is prepared from the dried inner bark of trees in the genus Cinnamomum.

question: What gas traditionally creates the holes in Swiss cheese?
note: Bacteria release carbon dioxide during ripening, forming the holes known as eyes.

question: Aquafaba, used as an egg-white substitute, is usually the cooking liquid from what?
note: Aquafaba is the protein- and starch-containing liquid left from cooking chickpeas or found in a can of them.

question: Cloves are dried parts of a tree. Which parts?
note: Cloves are the dried unopened flower buds of the clove tree.

question: Which cocoa component is absent from standard white chocolate?
note: White chocolate uses cocoa butter but contains no nonfat cocoa solids.

question: Brazil nuts develop inside what kind of structure?
note: A Brazil-nut tree produces a hard, woody fruit that holds numerous seeds arranged inside.

question: Tahini is a paste made chiefly from which seeds?
note: Tahini is made by grinding sesame seeds into a smooth paste.

question: Which part of broccoli do people mainly eat?
note: A broccoli head is a cluster of immature flower buds carried on branching stems.

question: Why are some traditional pretzels dipped in lye before baking?
note: The alkaline bath accelerates browning and creates the pretzel's distinctive crust and flavor.

question: A cat uses its whiskers mainly as what kind of tool?
note: Whiskers are specialized touch hairs that help cats sense nearby objects and air movement.

question: A shark's skeleton is made mostly from what?
note: Sharks and other elasmobranchs have skeletons made of cartilage rather than bone.

question: What shape are a goat's pupils in ordinary light?
note: Goats have horizontally elongated pupils that provide a broad view of their surroundings.

question: How does a frog take in most of the water it needs?
note: Frogs absorb water through a specialized patch of skin instead of drinking it normally.

question: Where does a sea otter often store food while diving?
note: Loose skin under each forearm forms a pocket where a sea otter can hold prey or a rock.

question: Which bird can sustain backward flight?
note: A hummingbird can reverse the angle of its wings to fly backward as well as hover.

question: Ants exchange oxygen without having which organs?
note: Ants have no lungs; air moves through tiny openings into a network of tracheal tubes.

question: What type of blood vessel carries blood away from the heart?
note: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, regardless of its oxygen content.

question: Which clear part of the eye has no blood vessels and gets oxygen mainly from tears and air?
note: The transparent cornea has no blood vessels; it receives oxygen from the air through the tear film.

question: Which tree appears at the center of Lebanon's national flag?
note: Lebanon's flag places a green cedar tree between two red horizontal bands.

question: Which city sits on both the European and Asian sides of the Bosporus?
note: The Bosporus divides Istanbul between a European shore and an Asian shore.

question: Which national flag includes an open Bible in its coat of arms?
note: The Dominican Republic's coat of arms, centered on its flag, includes an open Bible.

question: Which present-day country contains the ancient city of Petra?
note: The Nabataean rock-cut city of Petra lies in southern Jordan.

question: What was the main purpose of the Inca road system?
note: The Qhapaq Nan connected Inca territories for communication, trade, defense, and administration.

question: Why does the Eiffel Tower become slightly taller in hot weather?
note: Thermal expansion makes the iron structure grow by a few millimeters in summer heat.

question: Which U.S. state is both the westernmost and easternmost by longitude?
note: Alaska's Aleutian Islands cross the 180th meridian, placing the state in both east and west longitudes.

question: The ancient city of Timbuktu is in which modern country?
note: Timbuktu stands near the Niger River in the West African country of Mali.

question: The Rosetta Stone repeats one decree in how many writing systems?
note: The decree appears in hieroglyphic, Demotic, and ancient Greek scripts.

question: In Monopoly, may a player collect rent while in Jail?
note: The official rules allow a jailed player to buy and sell property, build, and collect rent.

question: How many points is a blank tile worth in Scrabble?
note: A blank may represent any letter but carries no point value.

question: In standard chess, can a pawn promote to a second queen?
option_d: Only if the first queen was captured
note: Promotion is not limited by pieces already on the board, so multiple queens are legal.

question: Where are the original stuffed toys that inspired Winnie-the-Pooh displayed?
note: Christopher Robin Milne's original Pooh, Tigger, Eeyore, Piglet, and Kanga toys are held by the New York Public Library.

question: What was Mario called in his first appearance in Donkey Kong?
note: The arcade character later known as Mario was originally identified as Jumpman.

question: Every standard Tetris piece is built from how many equal squares?
note: The name tetromino describes each shape made from four edge-connected squares.

question: In UNO, when may you legally play a Wild Draw Four card?
option_b: Only when you have no card matching the current color
answer: Only when you have no card matching the current color
note: The rules permit Wild Draw Four only when the player holds no card matching the current color.

question: What object carries the inscription "One Ring to rule them all" in Tolkien's story?
note: The fiery inscription appears on the One Ring when it is heated.

question: In the original Pac-Man arcade game, what restores one of the ghosts to normal after it is eaten?
option_a: Its eyes returning to the ghost house
answer: Its eyes returning to the ghost house
note: An eaten ghost's eyes travel back to the central ghost house, where the ghost regenerates.

question: What is the small sheath at the end of a shoelace called?
note: An aglet is the sheath that binds a shoelace end and helps it pass through eyelets.

question: QR codes were first developed to track parts in which industry?
note: DENSO WAVE developed the QR Code in 1994 to improve component tracking in automobile manufacturing.

question: In the original toilet-paper roll patent drawing, which way does the loose end hang?
note: Seth Wheeler's 1891 patent drawing shows the perforated paper feeding over the top of the roll.

question: Which came first: the metal food can or the can opener?
note: Canned food appeared decades before dedicated openers; early cans were opened with tools such as hammers and chisels.

question: What is the metal band that holds a pencil's eraser called?
note: The crimped metal sleeve joining an eraser to a pencil is called a ferrule.

question: In Grant Wood's American Gothic, what relationship did he imagine between the two figures?
note: Wood described the stern pair as a farmer and his adult daughter, not a married couple.

question: Rodin originally designed The Thinker as part of which larger work?
note: The seated poet first appeared above the doorway in Rodin's monumental Gates of Hell.

question: How many canvases make up Andy Warhol's Campbell's Soup Cans?
note: Warhol painted 32 separate canvases, one for each soup variety Campbell sold at the time.

question: In Edvard Munch's account behind The Scream, where did the scream come from?
note: Munch wrote that he sensed an infinite scream passing through nature while walking at sunset.

question: What does the zipper-maker name YKK abbreviate?
note: YKK comes from the former company name Yoshida Kogyo Kabushikikaisha.

question: Which film was the first animated feature nominated for the Academy Award for Best Picture?
option_a: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
note: Beauty and the Beast received a Best Picture nomination for the 1991 film year.

question: What everyday object does Doctor Who's TARDIS resemble from the outside?
note: Its faulty chameleon circuit leaves it disguised as a blue British police box.

question: Which feature film is credited with popularizing synchronized spoken dialogue?
note: The Jazz Singer, released in 1927, became the first feature-length motion picture with synchronized dialogue sequences.

question: At which televised event did Michael Jackson first perform his famous moonwalk?
note: Jackson unveiled the move during Billie Jean on the Motown 25 television special.

question: Who supplied the distinctive speaking voice of E.T. in E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial?
note: Pat Welsh provided E.T.'s principal speaking voice, with other sounds blended into the final track.

question: What text is absent from the front cover of the Beatles album Abbey Road?
option_a: The album title and band name
answer: The album title and band name
note: The iconic cover shows the four Beatles crossing Abbey Road without printing the band name or album title on the front.

question: In The Matrix, which pill does Neo take to learn the truth?
note: Neo chooses the red pill and wakes from the simulated world.

question: Which television comedy follows the employees of the fictional Dunder Mifflin paper company?
note: The US version of The Office centers on Dunder Mifflin's Scranton branch.

question: In soccer, can a player be penalized for offside directly from a goal kick?
note: The offside law specifically exempts players receiving the ball directly from a goal kick.

question: In baseball, what happens when a batter bunts a foul ball with two strikes?
note: Unlike an ordinary foul with two strikes, a foul bunt counts as strike three.

question: How many points are needed to win the deciding fifth set in indoor volleyball, barring deuce?
note: The deciding fifth set is played to 15 points, with a two-point winning margin.

question: Which restriction applies when castling in chess?
option_b: The king may not cross an attacked square
option_c: The queen must still be on the board
